proposals.relationship: As Deborah Simmons interprets his work, Adams draws on Fanon’s account of decolonization to connect autobiographical experiences of colonial alienation with collective historical struggle.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicitly mediated through Simmons’s 2002 tribute, pp. 6–7. Her reading connects Prison of Grass and Tortured People; their original and revised editions remain distinct. This is a specified intellectual resource, not an inference from Adams’s Marxist politics. The complete book bodies remain unread here.
primary_locators: Simmons, In Tribute to Howard Adams, printed pp. 6–7: narrative form, colonial space and the movement from personal alienation to historical becoming; notes 4–11 on p. 12.

proposals.relationship: Palmer uses Adams’s criticism of state-funded Indigenous leadership to develop his history of the linked struggles against capitalism and colonialism (2024).
proposals.evidence_note: A specifically used historical argument, not personal mentoring or wholesale endorsement. Palmer distinguishes Adams’s position from Harold Cardinal’s and also qualifies Adams’s overincarceration figures. The selected Palmer passages were freshly read; Adams’s cited book passages were not independently checked in their entirety.
primary_locators: The Past Is Before Us, printed pp. 299–300, especially the paragraph beginning Red Power militants such as Howard Adams and its continuation; note 80 on p. 300.
